summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming but called the task bounded ("This is bounded — one function, one caller, one file — so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec"). It gave the design in chat, took approval, and edited app.js. It never wrote a spec document, so it did not escalate to the architectural path.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. The agent explicitly chose the bounded path and wrote no spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ (no docs directory exists). It got approval for an in-chat design and went straight to editing app.js. This is exactly the failure the story describes.

observations.description: The router picked bounded for a request that literally asks to change a public function's signature (add a userId parameter to login) for cross-cutting tracking. It based the call on how small the current code is (one caller), not on how big the requested change is. That skipped the spec-doc path.

The agent did spot real complexity. It noted that a caller-supplied identity is an auth-bypass shape, and that real tracking would need wiring to API_ENDPOINT. It even said "If you want the real thing now, that's a bigger change... and I'd re-classify it." These signals of hidden complexity could be used to push it toward the architectural path instead of settling on a placeholder design.

The agent steered away from the literal request (add a parameter) and recommended keeping the signature unchanged and returning userId instead. That's sensible on security grounds, but it quietly redefines the task so it fits the bounded path.
On first launch, both the folder-trust dialog and the bypass-permissions dialog have 'No, exit' selected by default. This is expected Claude Code behaviour, but it takes an extra keypress on each.

criteria.evidence: The session log (jq over tool_use entries) shows the first tool call was {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. The Edit calls on app.js came later.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: Agent text in the log: "**This is bounded** — one function, one caller, one file — so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." Running `ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". `find coding-agent-workdir -path '*specs*'` returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: Spec document presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec document was written. The agent put the design in chat ("Here's the short design. Change — app.js only..." ending "Does this look right? I'll implement once you say yes.") and then made two Edit calls on app.js. `git status` shows only " M app.js".

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: The agent chose the bounded path in so many words: "This is bounded ... so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec". It then gave an in-chat design and never committed a spec file.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The agent never mentioned a spike or a probe plan. Its classification text says bounded and nothing else.
